facts.statement: The genus Cynodontosuchus was first described by Arthur Smith Woodward in 1896.
Cynodontosuchus was the first non-Cenozoic sebecosuchian to be described by Arthur Smith Woodward in 1896.
facts.quote: Cynodontosuchus was the first non-Cenozoic sebecosuchian to be described, being assigned to the suborder in 1896 by Arthur Smith Woodward.

facts.statement: The description of Cynodontosuchus was based on an incomplete snout and an articulated lower jaw.
facts.quote: It was described on the basis of an incomplete snout and articulated lower jaw.

facts.statement: Researchers have proposed that Cynodontosuchus is a senior synonym of the genus Baurusuchus.
facts.quote: It has been proposed several times that the genus is a senior synonym of Baurusuchus.

facts.statement: Cynodontosuchus differs from Baurusuchus by having a shallower rostrum and five maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: However, it differs from Baurusuchus in that its rostrum is less deep and has five maxillary teeth.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cynodontosuchus have been found in Argentina from the Bajo de la Carpa Formation (Santonian) and the Pichi Picun Leufu Formation (Coniacian and Santonian).
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from Argentina of Late Cretaceous age from the Bajo de la Carpa Formation (dating back to the Santonian), the Pichi Picun Leufu Formation (dating back to the Coniacian and Santonian).

facts.statement: Fossils of Cynodontosuchus have also been found in the Tiupampan Santa Lucía Formation of Bolivia.
facts.quote: the Tiupampan Santa Lucía Formation of Bolivia.

facts.statement: Cynodontosuchus lived between 85.7 and 61.66 million years ago, from the Santonian to the Danian.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Danian (85.7 to 61.66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Cynodontosuchus belongs to the family Baurusuchidae.
Cynodontosuchus is classified as a reptile.

rejected.statement: Cynodontosuchus possesses a large saber-like second maxillary tooth and a gap between the upper jaw bones that accommodates a large lower tooth.
rejected.quote: The presence of a large saber-like second maxillary tooth and a diastema between the maxilla and premaxilla that made room for a large mandibular tooth suggests that Cynodontosuchus is a member of the family Baurusuchidae.
